title: The Lion's Territory: A Daily Patrol

scenes.heading: A territory has boundaries
scenes.caption: A lion's range is a living map
scenes.narration: A lion's territory is more than a patch of land. It is a living map of water, shade, prey and safe resting places. Knowing this landscape can make the difference between survival and exhaustion.

scenes.heading: The patrol begins
scenes.caption: Familiar paths are checked again and again
scenes.narration: As the day begins, a male lion moves along familiar routes. He does not need to race. A steady patrol lets him inspect the edges of his range while conserving energy in the growing heat.

scenes.heading: Scent leaves a message
scenes.caption: Scent marks communicate presence
scenes.narration: At prominent trees and bushes, lions may rub their faces or leave scent marks. These chemical signals carry information to other lions, helping communicate who has been using the area.

scenes.heading: Listen before moving on
scenes.caption: Sounds reveal activity beyond the grass
scenes.narration: The lion pauses. A distant call, movement in the grass or the smell of another animal can change what happens next. A successful patrol depends as much on attention as on strength.

scenes.heading: Rivals test the boundary
scenes.caption: Territory can bring costly conflict
scenes.narration: Neighbouring lions may challenge the edges of a range. Roaring can advertise presence and help avoid a dangerous encounter, but if rivals meet, defending territory can demand energy and carry real risk.

scenes.heading: The route continues
scenes.caption: Patrolling protects access to vital resources
scenes.narration: The lion moves on through the grass, checking another familiar path. Territory is never permanently secure. By patrolling, marking and responding to rivals, lions help protect access to the resources their pride depends on.
